transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

The clinic was concerned about how little I’ve been eating. Most days I just have coffee before the warehouse, maybe a yogurt or a few bites after GED class. A real meal just feels like it throws off everything I’m trying to keep in line.
When you think about eating a full meal, are you worried about gaining weight?
Yeah. If I eat fried food from the break room, or a big plate at church, I get scared it’s going to show on me right away. Then I can’t stop thinking about it and I want to check the scale.
Do you ever have times where you lose control and eat an unusually large amount of food in a short period?
No, I don’t think so. I usually try not to let myself get to that point.
Could you tell me your current height and weight?

I don’t know my exact height or weight right now. I know my work pants are getting loose, and people keep saying I look too thin, but when the number goes down it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.
If you menstruate, have your periods been regular, or have they stopped or changed recently?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t been keeping track of it closely.
About how much did the scale say the last time you checked your weight?

I don’t remember the exact number. I just know it had gone down, and that felt like I was finally making progress. Even though my pants are loose and people say I look too thin, I don’t feel like I should have to gain it back.
Do you ever make yourself throw up, or use things like laxatives or diet pills, to control your weight?
I’m not sure what you mean by diet pills. I haven’t really thought of it as doing anything like that.
Did the clinic tell you what your weight was when you were there?

They may have, but I wasn’t really focused on the exact number. I just knew it was lower, and honestly that felt like I was finally getting somewhere. My work pants are loose and people say I’m too thin, but I don’t see why I should have to put the weight back on.
Do you push yourself to exercise or stay physically active specifically to burn calories or lose weight?
I’m not sure. I’m active sometimes, but I don’t really think about it in terms of burning calories.
When you look at yourself in the mirror, do you see yourself as being overweight or having parts of your body that are too large?

Yeah. Before class or softball, I’ll look in the mirror and my stomach and thighs still seem bigger than they should be. It can kind of decide how I feel about the whole day—like I’m doing okay or like I’m failing.
Have you ever used water pills or diuretics to try to control your weight?
No, I haven’t used water pills.
About how much weight have you lost since this started?

I don’t know the exact amount. My work pants are loose now, and people keep saying I look too thin, but when the number goes down, it feels like I’m finally getting somewhere. I don’t really see why I should have to put it back on.
Do you ever make yourself vomit after eating to control your weight?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I haven’t really noticed that being something I do.
Did the doctors or staff at the clinic tell you that you are underweight?
Yeah, the doctor and people from church have said they’re worried I’m underweight. I just think they’re making it bigger than it is. I’m still working, doing my classes, and keeping up with my life.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient demonstrates intentional restriction of energy intake leading to being noticeably underweight according to clinic staff and peers, accompanied by an intense fear of weight gain and body image distortion (perceiving stomach and thighs as too big despite loose clothing and low weight). The patient denies binge eating and compensatory purging behaviors, consistent with the restricting type of Anorexia Nervosa (ICD-10 F50.0).

confirmed_symptoms: Severe restriction of food intake (consuming mostly coffee and yogurt)
Noticeable weight loss leading to loose-fitting clothes
Clinically confirmed underweight status by medical clinic and peers
Intense fear of weight gain and dread of fatness
Distorted body image (perceiving stomach and thighs as too big despite being underweight)
Overvaluation of weight and shape on self-worth
Denial of the medical seriousness of low body weight and resistance to weight gain

additional_requirements: Absence of regular self-induced vomiting or diuretic/laxative misuse
